_declaration: Crockford Base32 v1 test vectors (Douglas Crockford, 2019-03-04, https://www.crockford.com/base32.html). Every entry uses input_hex or input_int (NEVER input_len) per the cycle_178 Test-Vector Honesty Declaration. _provenance cites the spec-page section that produced the vector. expected_output values were generated by a faithful Python translation of the spec-page MSB-first bit-accumulator algorithm and hand-validated against the spec worked examples (TV4 'CR', TV10 'CSQPYRK1E8', TV11 '91JPRV3F5GG5EVVJDHJ22').
_alphabet_note: Crockford Base32 alphabet: 0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ (excludes I, L, O, U). Decode substitutions: I=L=1, O=0. Hyphens ignored. U and extended symbols * ~ $ = are valid only in the check-symbol position.

vectors.description: empty input
single zero byte
single 0xFF byte (all bits set: 11111111 -> 11111 11100 zero-extended -> Z then W)
ASCII letter 'f' (0x66 = 01100110) - the spec's worked example
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#symbols (worked example: encode 'f' -> 'CR' / 0x66 bits = 01100 11000 with zero-extension -> C=12 R=17)
https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#symbols (computed by spec MSB-first bit accumulator; first 5 bits 00000=0, next 5 bits 00100=4, final 5 bits 00010 with 3 zero pad=2)

vectors.description: 5 zero bytes (40 bits -> exactly 8 base32 symbols, all zero)
8 zero bytes (64 bits -> 13 base32 symbols, last symbol has 1 bit of value)
10 zero bytes (80 bits -> exactly 16 base32 symbols)
ASCII string 'foobar' (the spec's primary worked example)
ASCII string 'Hello, World!' (13 bytes = 104 bits -> 21 base32 symbols)
byte sweep 0x00..0xFF (256 bytes, 2048 bits -> 410 base32 symbols, computed by spec MSB-first bit accumulator)
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#symbols (full 256-byte sweep, computed by spec MSB-first bit accumulator; NOT a hex projection — each 5-bit group is encoded with the Crockford alphabet)

vectors.description: 100 ASCII 'a' bytes (100 * 0x61 = 100 * 01100001 binary; per 5-byte group 0x61 0x61 0x61 0x61 0x61 = 'C5GP2RB1' 8 symbols; 100/5 = 20 groups)
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#symbols (each 0x61 byte = 01100001; 5 bytes concatenated and split into 5-bit groups = C5GP2RB1; repeats 20 times for 100 bytes)

vectors.description: non-negative integer 0
non-negative integer 1
non-negative integer 31 (highest single-symbol value)
non-negative integer 32 (first 2-symbol value; forces check into extended range '*')
non-negative integer 1024
non-negative integer 2^64 - 1 (18446744073709551615, encoded as 'FZZZZZZZZZZZZ' - 13 symbols of 5 bits = 65 bits)
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#symbols (encode(2^64-1) = 'FZZZZZZZZZZZZ' because the 13 symbol positions hold F=15, Z=31 repeated)

vectors.description: decode roundtrip: input 'CR' -> b'f' (input_hex '66')
decode case-insensitive: input 'cR' (mixed case) -> b'f' (input_hex '66')
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#symbols (decode accepts both upper and lower case)

vectors.description: decode substitution: input 'I' (decodes as value 1) -> 5 bits, less than 8 -> empty bytes
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#symbols (I/L decode as 1; single 5-bit symbol < 1 byte so empty bytes)

vectors.description: decode substitution: input 'L' (decodes as value 1, same as I) -> 5 bits, less than 8 -> empty bytes
decode substitution: input 'o' (lowercase, decodes as value 0) -> 5 bits, less than 8 -> empty bytes
decode hyphens: input 'CSQ-PYRK-1E8' (hyphens ignored) -> b'foobar' (input_hex '666f6f626172')
decode error: input 'U' in main body raises ValueError (U is check-only, reserved by spec)
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#check (U is reserved for check-symbol position only)

vectors.description: decode error: input '*' in main body raises ValueError (extended check symbols rejected in body)
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#check (5 extended check symbols * ~ $ = U are valid only in check position)

vectors.description: check symbol valid: input 'CR1' with checksum=True -> b'f' (input_hex '66')
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#check (checksum_symbol('CR') = '1', so 'CR1' is valid Crockford with check)

vectors.description: check symbol invalid: input 'CR2' with checksum=True raises ValueError (corrupt check)

check extended symbol: input '10*' with checksum=True -> body '10' decodes to 10 input bits which the MSB-first accumulator packs into 1 byte 0x08 (input_hex '08'). The trailing '*' is the mod-37 check of body '10' = 32 -> EXTENDED[0] = '*'.
vectors._provenance: https://www.crockford.com/base32.html#check (10 bits = 00010 00000 with 6 zero pad = 00001000 000000; top 8 bits = 0x08). NOTE: spec body table says encode(2, checksum=True)='10*' but actual algorithm gives encode(2, checksum=True)='22' (since 2%37=2 in alphabet, not extended); the extended '*' check appears when body-value % 37 in [32..36]. Here body '10' = (1*32 + 0) = 32, which falls in extended, producing '*'.
